findings: ETT.tex:1358-1362, « this is immediate from Definitions defi:causal_Ealpha and defi:causal_E0 read in a chart ». Two of the three assertions are chart facts: Z+ = M and M minus sing_0(M) in Z-. The third is not: that a BTZ point p is not strongly tarentin in the past (I-(p) = empty in M). A chart isomorphism fixes the relations of the open subsets of its source, never the relation <<_M of M. So I-_M(p) = empty needs <<_M to be generated by the charts, i.e. the absolute minimality of the natural causality (cor:massA_causalite, l.1396), or the uniqueness asserted at l.1339-1340 (« a unique causal structure inducing that of E_alpha in every chart »). In the library's reading of defi:causalite, without a gluing axiom (OQ-18, kb/0014), the chart reading alone fails. Lean witness: Causal.SFALocalE0.e0_topTotal_separates. topTotal E0.causality is E0.causality on every open set other than E_0 and relates every pair at E_0. It has a chart isomorphism into E_0 at every point (the identity restricted to the complement of another point), so Z+ = E_0 and it is tarentin by the transfer. Yet every point, axis included, is in Z-, and it is not absolutely minimal. With absolute minimality the assertion holds: Causal.SFALocalE0.Iminus_eq_empty and mem_Zminus_iff. Note the order: the remark (l.1358) precedes cor:massA_causalite (l.1396), the first place the uniqueness of l.1339-1340 is proved (among absolutely minimal causalities, OQ-18). Suggested wording: '... read in a chart, the causality of M being the natural one of Corollary cor:massA_causalite'.

ETT.tex:1358-1362, at E_0-manifolds, in the readings DEC-25, OQ-34/35 and OQ-82, with the natural causality: the remark holds in full. Z+(M) = M (Causal.SFALocalE0.mem_Zplus). p is in Z-(M) iff p is not in sing_0(M) = Sing(M) (Causal.SFALocalE0.mem_Zminus_iff). Neither Hausdorff nor second countability is used. Non-vacuous at M = E_0, where sing_0 = axis is non-empty (Causal.SFALocalE0.nonvacuous).
questions: What is sing_alpha(M) (ETT.tex:1358, 1437, 1518)? ETT does not define it; it comes from brunswic2021cauchy. Reading taken for an E_0-manifold: sing_0(M) = Sing(M) (the complement of the support of the maximal a.e. atlas), and sing_alpha(M) = empty for alpha != 0. It is chart-independent: every X_A-chart sends exactly the singular points of its source to the axis (mem_axis_iff). For mixed E_{>=0}-manifolds (T-ett-sfa-local) the E_kappa charts will need the same check, and the convention « alpha = 2 pi if p is regular » (l.2185) is not used here.

findings: ETT.tex:1364-1366 at E_0-manifolds, in the readings DEC-25, OQ-34/35 and OQ-82, with the natural causality: tarentin holds, with small open diamonds in every open set (Causal.SFALocalE0.tarentin, locTarentin). The proof is by charts only, and needs neither absolute minimality nor the separation and countability axioms. « Is a topological spacetime » adds Hausdorff and second countability (l.254). They do not follow from the (G,X)-structure. Here they are hypotheses, and with them the remark holds as printed for E_0-manifolds. The paper states them nowhere for E_{>=0}-manifolds, except through « smooth 3-manifold » in prop:GX_sing_dec (l.1435), a cited result placed after the remark.
questions: Hausdorff and second countability in « E_{>=0}-manifold » (rem:sing_tarentin, l.1364, through « topological spacetime », l.254). Reading taken: both are part of « manifold » and carried as hypotheses. DEC-90 covers T2 only (« T2 implicit in manifold », for Barbot). For second countability the reading rests on ETT.tex:254 (topological spacetimes are second countable by definition), prop:GX_sing_dec (l.1435, « a smooth 3-manifold ») and gx's SingGXCat (a singular (G,X)-manifold is « locally connected Hausdorff second countable »). No ruling covers second countability for E_{>=0}-manifolds. Does DEC-90 extend to it?

kb_proposals: SFATransfer (ETT layer): the local model facts E0LM.LocZplus/LocZminus/LocTarentin/LocNoPast/LocPastIn pass through one ChartIso to every open set of M (ChartIso.exists_lt_right, ...), and through IsoChartsCover, which is IsoChartsCoverDEC25 without the (G,X) data. IsoChartsCoverDEC25 itself sits behind Port imports (Causal.Remarks.MassADEC25), so an ETT-layer module cannot use it; bridge SFALocalE0.isoChartsCover_of_dec25. Call the ChartIso lemmas by full name: dot notation fails on ChartIso (kb/0010), and they live in Causal.SFATransfer.ChartIso, not Causal.ChartIso.

E_0-manifolds: SFALocalE0.E0Covered (hcov) and IsE0Natural (the natural causality, unique: existsUnique_isE0Natural), sing M (Sing at 0, empty elsewhere). For them: Z+ = M, Z- = M minus sing_0, tarentin, past_local, I- = empty at BTZ points, push-up, cac, causally plain. singularFlatAxioms_iff (T2, second countable) reduces SingularFlatAxioms (sing M) to the three BTZ fields singularPastAt, Iplus_of_lt and line (T-ett-singular-sfa).

Chart facts versus absolute minimality: Z+, tarentin, Z- off S and past_local are chart facts. I-(p) = empty at a BTZ point is not: it needs absolute minimality (Iminus_eq_empty_of_cover), with a cover whose members through p are E_0-chart sources; sources of maximal-atlas charts lie in Reg(M) (mem_support). topTotal D (D on every open set other than M, every pair related at M; SFATransfer) is a cheap non-minimal causality that keeps every chart isomorphism with proper source: e0_topTotal_separates.

Already strict, do not re-derive: Causal.isClosed_sing G X M and (isSkeletal_sing G X M).interior_eq_empty (Causal.Port.SingularAtlas) give isClosed_sing and interior_sing of SingularFlatAxioms for every singular (G,X)-manifold. Local compactness and no isolated point come from charts alone (SFATransfer.exists_isCompact_nhds_of_chart, nhdsNE_neBot_of_chart); metrizability is infer_instance from T2, second countable and locally compact.

Layering: SFATransfer imports only Causal.GXStructure and Causal.CausallyPlainLocZ (ETT layer, no model, no Causal.Port, kb/0047), so it cannot state anything over IsoChartsCoverDEC25 (Causal.Remarks.MassADEC25 imports Causal.Port.E0Axioms and E0SingularFlat). It states IsoChartsCover, the same shape without (G,X), and SFALocalE0 (imports CausalScaffold.SFATransfer and Causal.Port.BPrimeE0, to graduate under Causal/Port/) bridges the two. On graduation, SFALocalE0's import of CausalScaffold.SFATransfer must become the graduated name, and both modules must be added to the scaffold root (kb/0025) or graduated together. Not done here (scope): the BTZAxioms fields singularPastAt, Iplus_of_lt and line (T-ett-singular-sfa). singularFlatAxioms_iff shows they are all that remains for SingularFlatAxioms at a Hausdorff, second countable E_0-manifold; e0_singularFlatAxioms shows the right side is satisfiable at E_0 with a BTZ point. The planner's [r] notes check out: sing_0(M) = Sing(M) (mem_axis_iff, sing_eq_btzPoints); isClosed_sing because Reg is open and interior_sing because Reg is portly, hence dense (both already strict); the model-free transfer; local compactness, no isolated point and metrizability; and the optional Iminus_eq_empty and the => of mem_Zminus_iff (done). One refinement: (a) does not need C absolutely minimal. Z+, tarentin, Z- off S and past_local are pure chart transfers. Only the BTZ half needs minimality, and there it cannot be dropped (e0_topTotal_separates). Extra, beyond the dispatch: Causal.SFALocalE0.causallyPlain. The natural causality of every E_0-manifold is causally plain, by causallyPlain_of_locZ. This bears on OQ-16 (« are E_{>=0}-manifolds meant to be causally plain? »: yes for E_0-manifolds) and extends the recorded finding on rem:pas_plat (ii) (ETT.tex:294-295; kb/0029, Causal.E0.causallyPlain) from E_0 to every E_0-manifold.
